podcast.title: Fatal Boating Accident in Cozumel (December 2000)
podcast.body: On December 18, 2000, while scuba diving with her sons and dive master Ivan Diaz off Cozumel's Chunkanab reef, a national marine park restricted to power boats, Kirsty MacColl was struck and killed instantly by the propellers of a 31-foot motorboat named the "Percolito." The boat, powered by 315 horsepower engines, roared through the restricted area as MacColl surfaced, and she managed to push her 15-year-old son Jamie out of the way just before impact, sustaining severe head and chest injuries that virtually severed her body. "Just after 2pm, just as Kirstie came to the surface after the first of two planned dives, a 31-foot motorboat called the Percolito came roaring through this restricted area with its 315 horsepower engines. Kirstie was right in the way. She pushed her 15-year-old son Jamie out of the way just in time, but the boat hit her in the head and caused severe chest injuries. She was killed instantly by the props."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tragic Death in Cozumel, Mexico - December 18, 2000
podcast.body: While on holiday in Cozumel, Mexico, with her new partner, James Knight, and her sons, Kirsty was scuba diving in a prohibited area for watercraft on December 18, 2000. She was hit by a speeding boat while surfacing, killing her instantly, after she pushed her son Jamie out of the way. "In December of 2000, she and her new partner, a guy named James Knight, took Kristi's sons to Cosmell, Mexico. On December the 18th, she and the boys were diving in an area where water craft, any kind of boats, were strictly prohibited. But just as they were surfacing from a deep dive, a speed boat tore through the area. Right on top of Kristi and her son, Jamie. Now Kristi was able to see the boat coming and push Jamie out of the way, but as she did, the boat hit her, killing her instantly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: BBC Documentary and Book About Her Death
podcast.body: The details behind Kirsty MacColl's death are explored in a BBC documentary titled "Who Killed Kristi McCall" and a book by her sister, Jean, called "Sun on the Water, the brilliant life and tragic death of Kristi McCall." "If you're interested in the details behind Kristi's death, there's a BBC documentary called Who Killed Kristi McCall. And there's a book called Sun on the Water, the brilliant life and tragic death of Kristi McCall by her sister, Jean."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Boat Owner and Driver - Guillermo Gonzales Nova, Jose Senyem
podcast.body: The boat involved in the accident was owned by Mexican millionaire Guillermo Gonzales Nova, who made his wealth in supermarkets. Although Nova and his family were on board, an employee named Jose Senyem was allegedly driving, a claim disputed by eyewitnesses who reported the boat was traveling much faster than the claimed one knot. "The boat was owned by a Mexican millionaire who made all his money in supermarkets. His name is Guillermo Gonzales Nova. Although he wasn't at the helm of the boat at the time of the accident, he and his family were on board. Driving the boat was apparently an employee named Jose Senyem. Although there are a number of eyewitnesses that dispute that. Witnesses say the boat was going much faster than what had been claimed."

podcast.title: Collaborations and Songwriting - Johnny Marr, Bette Midler, BBC
podcast.body: She recorded with Johnny Marr of The Smiths and frequently offered input and advice during U2 recording sessions. MacColl also wrote a couple of songs for Bette Midler and had one of her songs adapted as a theme for a BBC TV show. "She recorded with Johnny Marr of The Smiths and Kristi was known to hang around YouTube recording sessions offering input and advice. She also wrote a couple of songs for Bett Middler and had one of her songs adapted as a theme for a BBC TV show."

podcast.title: Collaborations with Shane MacGowan
podcast.body: Kirsty MacColl is widely recognized for her celebrated duet with Shane MacGowan on The Pogues' song "Fairytale of New York." "She's the woman who duets with Shane McGowan on the Pog's Fairy Tale of New York."

podcast.title: Controversial Legal Outcome of Death
podcast.body: The "Percolito" was owned and captained by Mexican millionaire Guillermo Gonzales Nova, who initially admitted to being at the helm and was seen in handcuffs, but the story later changed to an employee, Jose Sen Yam, being the pilot. Despite eyewitnesses disputing this, Sen Yam, a deckhand without proper documents, was arrested and found guilty of "culpable homicide" under Mexican law, receiving a sentence of two years ten months. However, he avoided jail by paying a $90 USD fine and was ordered to pay just over $2,100 in restitution based on his salary, leading to widespread suspicion of a payoff for taking the blame. "Although he first apparently admitted to being at the helm with the time of the accident, he was seen being let away from the scene in handcuffs. The story later changed. The news story was that a 26-year-old employee named Jose Sen Yam was actually piloting the boat at the time of the accident, although there are a number of eyewitnesses who dispute that, including Diaz, the dive master." "Jose was arrested and found guilty of something known under Mexican law as culpable homicide, the sentence two years ten months. However, the law also said he could avoid jail time if he simply paid a fine, and that fine was about $90 USD."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Justice for Kirsty Campaign
podcast.body: Kirsty MacColl's family launched the "Justice for Kirsty" campaign, lobbying Mexican authorities, making applications to human rights councils, and securing support from U2 to pressure the government after a judge was found to have mishandled the case. Despite their efforts, the campaign closed in December 2009, having exhausted all possible avenues without achieving further legal recourse. "Cursedy's family created something called the Justice for Cursedy campaign and began pressing the Mexican authorities to do something."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Justice for Kirsty Campaign - Ongoing Fight for Justice
podcast.body: Kirsty's family launched the "Justice for Kirsty" campaign, lobbying Mexican authorities and applying to human rights councils for further investigation. A judge in the case was found to have made errors, and U2 also supported the government in seeking the truth, but Mexican authorities have been unhelpful, leaving the true nature of her death unresolved. "Kristi's family created something called the Justice for Kristi campaign and began pressuring the Mexican authorities to do something. They made applications to human rights councils. A judge in the case was found to have made mistakes in his handling of the situation and you too is pushed for the government to get to the bottom of what happened. So far though, nothing. Mexican authorities have not been helpful at all."

podcast.title: Legal Proceedings and Controversial Sentence
podcast.body: Jose Senyem was arrested and found guilty of "culpable homicide" under Mexican law, receiving a sentence of two years and ten months. However, he avoided jail time by paying a fine of approximately $90 US dollars and was ordered to pay restitution based on his salary, totaling just over $2,100, fueling whispers of a payoff for taking the fall. "He was arrested and found guilty of something known under Mexican law as culpable homicide. The sentence was two years and ten months. The law also said that he could avoid jail time if he simply paid a fine. That fine was about $90 US dollars. He was also ordered to pay restitution to Kristi's family, but that restitution was based on his salary. The total came to just over $2,100. Meanwhile there were whispers that Senyem got a big payoff from someone for taking the fall."

xref.title: Steve Lillywhite's Role
xref.body: Producer Steve Lillywhite, known for his work on U2's first three albums, played a crucial role in the development of "Fairy Tale of New York." He produced The Pogues' third album, "If I Should Fall From Grace With God," and, being married to Kirsty MacColl, arranged for her to record the female vocal parts. "The producer was a guy named Steve Lillie White. He had helped you too with their first three albums."
